target_customer: Professionals who spend time on email, admin and web apps
problem: Knowledge workers lose time on email and admin work; Zuni offers an AI assistant that uses open tab context and, per its site, agents for professional work.
business_model: Consumer or prosumer AI assistant, pricing not found

founders.name: George Seabridge
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only the tagline Building AI agents for professional work. A secondary profile names Will Taylor as co-founder; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Chrome extension with LLM API calls over page context is standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Thin wrapper over frontier models that large browser and email vendors can match.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No outcome documented; incumbents shipped built in assistants.

market_need_then: No direct evidence found; general demand for AI email and browser assistants.

branding.domain_note: Uses zuni.app; Old House Labs listed as parent

identity.voice_and_tone: Terse tagline AI agents for high-value professional work

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; the name collides with Zuni Pueblo and other uses in search.

outcome_analysis: Zuni is listed active with one or two people and a minimal site. Descriptions vary between a Chrome sidebar copilot and AI agents for professional work, suggesting positioning changes over time that are undated. No traction, revenue or funding beyond aggregator-listed YC money was verified, so the outcome is unknown.
notes: Aggregators list a $500K YC pre-seed Sep 2024; unverified, no later round found. Extruct lists $7.2M revenue, implausible and ignored. Positioning conflict: YC description (Chrome extension with sidebar) versus current YC text and site (agents); a 2025 Show HN repost titled AI Copilot for the Browser exists. Location conflict London versus San Francisco. Team size listed as 1 or 2. Completeness pass: search for funding found no source for any round, so none recorded.
